title: Gulf Coast On High Alert as Rapidly Intensifying Hurricane Isaias Threatens Landfall
snippet: States of emergency and expanding evacuation orders stretch from Florida to Alabama as Hurricane Isaias rapidly gains strength in the Gulf, taking aim at a Friday night landfall.
content:
GULF SHORES, Ala. — Hurricane Isaias rapidly intensified into a formidable Category 2 storm in the Gulf of Mexico on Thursday, prompting widespread evacuation orders and emergency declarations across three Southeastern states ahead of an anticipated weekend landfall.

Packing sustained winds of 105 mph, the first Atlantic hurricane of the season is tracking northeast at 14 mph. Forecasters at the National Hurricane Center (NHC) warned the storm could briefly reach Category 3 intensity before taking direct aim at the northern Gulf Coast, with landfall targeted between Gulf Shores, Alabama, and Pensacola, Florida, late Friday or early Saturday morning.

Evacuations Expand Ahead of Landfall

In response to the escalating threat, Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis, Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey, and Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp declared states of emergency. Officials across the region are imploring residents in low-lying and coastal areas to finalize emergency preparations and obey evacuation instructions without delay.

Mandatory evacuations have taken effect for Walton County in Florida, alongside critical coastal zones in Okaloosa and Escambia counties, as well as Alabama's Dauphin Island. Meanwhile, popular tourist hubs like Orange Beach and Gulf Shores have instructed all non-resident visitors to leave the coast immediately.

"If you are in the Panhandle, assume that you are going to lose power," Gov. DeSantis warned during a news briefing, emphasizing the need for residents to stock up on basic supplies and fuel.

Dangerous Storm Surge and Flooding Risk

Meteorologists warn that Isaias presents a life-threatening combination of storm surge, severe inland flooding, and destructive winds. A Storm Surge Warning spans from the mouth of the Mississippi River to Florida's Big Bend, with peak surges expected to reach 5 to 7 feet around Mobile Bay and the Florida Panhandle.

The Weather Prediction Center has highlighted a Level 3 out of 4 risk for flash flooding across Mobile and the Panhandle, with widespread rainfall estimates of 6 to 10 inches. Outer rainbands spinning off the hurricane are also expected to trigger isolated tornadoes across southern Alabama and Northwest Florida as the storm pushes inland.

Energy Rigs Shut Down, Schools Close

The rapidly churning storm has already prompted precautionary action from energy producers. Major oil giants, including Shell, Chevron, and BP, have initiated shut-in protocols across multiple offshore facilities in the Gulf and evacuated non-essential crews.

On shore, school districts across more than a dozen counties in Alabama and Florida canceled classes through Friday, while several major universities shut down their campuses as residents prepare for sustained power outages and dangerous travel conditions.
